title: Case Sensitivity on Linux can break Steam Cloud Syncing for the `user://` folder
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in 4.8dev4 ### System information Godot v4.8.dev4 - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Fri, 21 Aug 2026 22:18:59 +0000 on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors (2880x1800 @ 120.00 Hz, 3840x2160 @ 240.00 Hz) - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Laptop GPU - Intel(R) Core(TM) Ultra 9 185H (22 threads) - 30.73 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description Windows and Mac have the `user://` folder pointing to `%APPDATA%\Godot` and `~/Library/Application Support/Godot`. So both are upper case `Godot`. Now if you are on either of these systems, you would set up the Cloud save paths of Steam (and other storefronts probably) to point to this folder: and then you can overwrite what the `WinAppDataRoaming` means on other platforms like this: Now the issue is, that if you set it up with upper case `Godot`, the syncing doesn't work on Linux. Steam Cloud first creates (if it doesn't exist) and syncs the cloud saves into `~/.local/share/Godot/`. Afterwards the game is started and Godot creates the `~/.local/share/godot/` folder and uses that one. This results in the Cloud saves not being picked up by the game. Interesting detail: Steam Cloud only creates the folder if no other Godot folder exists in that folder (without taking any key sensitivity into account). So if you previously started the editor or another Godot game, it will sync into the lower case folder. This can be currently fixed by setting the Steam Cloud Save path to a lower case `godot` folder. However, now on Mac and Windows the folder is lower case and thus different then in the [docs](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/io/data_paths.html). Additionally, if you have no Linux device to test the syncing on, you probably release the game with broken syncing. Different solutions: * Make Godot on Linux first check if any Godot folder exists and reuse that one without taking sensitivity into account. Goes against the expected value from the docs. * Make "Use Custom User Dir" Project Setting activated by default for template exports. However, may confuse Godot users because it doesn't behave the same in the editor as in the exported game. * Have a small dedicated section to Cloud Save syncing in the Godot docs. If I remember correctly, it would break in the same way for the Epic store cloud setup. * Switch to upper case `Godot` folder in general for Linux. Probably to big of a change for the engine. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Set up the Cloud Sync as detailed above. 2. Start the game on Windows and ensure a save is created. 3. Quit the game and make sure the save was synced. 4. On a Linux device, ensure no `~.local/share/godot/` folder exists (with any kind of capitalization) 5. Start the game, make sure it created a save and quit it again. 6. Now you should have a `~.local/share/godot/` and a `~.local/share/Godot/` folder. The first containing the local save and the second the Cloud Sync. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) Any kind of project hat writes data into `user://` is enough.
